claim: The Resource Groups Tagging API GetResources operation supports all resource types and returns the tagged or previously tagged resources in the specified Region for the account, and AWS WAF lets you tag web ACLs, rule groups, IP sets, and regex pattern sets through its API (not through the AWS WAF console); so a tagged AWS WAF IP set is a resource type that GetResources supports.
question: Does the Resource Groups Tagging API GetResources operation return AWS WAF (wafv2) IP sets, so that a task can verify its cleanup with a tag filter task=<task id>?

values.display: web ACLs, rule groups, IP sets

qualifiers.scope: Resource Groups Tagging API GetResources; AWS WAF (current API) IP sets that carry the tag
qualifiers.condition: the IP set carries the tag; GetResources looks only in the Region of the call

evidence.quote: The `GetResources`, `GetTagKeys`, and `GetTagValues` operations support all resource types.
Returns all the tagged or previously tagged resources that are located in the specified AWS Region for the account.
You can tag the AWS resources that you manage through AWS WAF: web ACLs, rule groups, IP sets, and regex pattern sets.

note: requests-08 for fr-0039 (task edge-protection-t01 verify step). The WAF developer guide has no tagging page (tagging.html redirects to what-is-aws-waf; saved snapshot empty), so the WAF API reference TagResource page is the service-side source. The saved Tagging API Welcome snapshot ends at the I entries, before AWS WAF; its only GetResources exceptions are IAM users and roles and EC2 Auto Scaling groups. The Resource Groups supported-resources table lists only AWS::WAF and AWS::WAFRegional (Classic) types, no AWS::WAFv2 types, so that table is not used. GetResources is Regional, so the verify call must run in the Region where the task created the IP set.
